proposal.title: 1978–79 external peripherals — video and printing terminals 2
proposal.reason: Import 9 distinct commercial identities from research items 161, 162, 163, 164, 165, 166, 167, 174, 175. Describe the native host boundary and assess product and core-standard impacts at 1979-12-31. Dedicated memory and other unrelated accessories explicitly carry no direct impact. Conditional comparisons do not establish qualified adapters, provider adoption or measured sales. Prices and cumulative sales remain editorial evidence, outside foundation and the annual-sales model. See the per-item evidence in data_storytelling/review_evidence/external-peripherals-1979/assessment.json. Revised for explicit product/standard relationships: consolidate descriptions into specification, relocate impact prose, compare canonical implementation boundaries and retain source/qualification limits. Historical documentation cannot establish fictional implementations or measured adoption. Per-record evidence: data_storytelling/review_evidence/external-impact-revision/assessment.json.

specification.description: 80 × 24 display, editing functions and additional screen memory. The intended host environment is {host}. Interfaces, cabling and software must match that configuration.

impacted_standards.assumption_description: Assess {historical_product} in its recorded {host} configuration. Compare complete console configurations on a host supporting both purchase paths.
impacted_standards.comparison_description: The terminal contains its own display controller and communicates through a serial interface instead of the Logix monitor link. The relationship concerns alternative complete configurations, not proven direct compatibility with this standard.
impacted_standards.outcomes_description: It supplies a mature alternative console and may reduce demand for a Logix card/monitor pair. This is competition between complete configurations, not a digital-link compatibility claim.

impacted_products.assumption_description: Assess the recorded {host} configuration with its required controller, cabling and software. 80 × 24 display, editing functions and additional screen memory.
impacted_products.comparison_description: The alternative uses the Aurelia video controller, 16 KiB local video memory and separate sprite storage. It needs a qualified digital monitor; 80-column output requires a compatible 640-pixel display. Its console configuration also needs input hardware. It includes no monitor or FlexiBUS ports. Competition is at complete-console level; the terminal does not separately replace both a keyboard and a video card in an already assembled system. The canonical implementation is {implementation}.
impacted_products.outcomes_description: A self-contained serial terminal can provide an S-100 computer’s console without an internal Logix video card and digital monitor. This is a conditional purchase-path assessment, not evidence of measured market share or superior performance.

impacted_products.assumption_description: Assess the recorded {host} configuration with its required controller, cabling and software. 80 × 24 display, editing functions and additional screen memory.
impacted_products.comparison_description: The alternative is a FlexiBUS keyboard, not a complete terminal. Compare a working console including host, display and interface; a conventional keyboard or terminal is not directly attachable through the keyboard device protocol. Competition is at complete-console level; the terminal does not separately replace both a keyboard and a video card in an already assembled system. The canonical implementation is {implementation}.
impacted_products.outcomes_description: The terminal includes its own keyboard. It competes as part of an alternative complete console, not as an electrically interchangeable keyboard. This is a conditional purchase-path assessment, not evidence of measured market share or superior performance.

impacted_products.assumption_description: Assess the recorded {host} configuration with its required controller, cabling and software. Approximately 30 characters/s; keyboard and selectable character spacing.
impacted_products.comparison_description: The alternative combines the MPI MP40 mechanism with a FlexiBUS device controller. Compare actual print width, character repertoire, quality, paper handling and qualified driver support; the current definition establishes no universal speed or output-quality advantage. It is a broader purchase than a printer and is not a plug-compatible FlexiPrint40 replacement.
